chunks: 4417 - Dawud ibn Sirhan narrated from Zurarah, from Abi Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress—none marries her except an adulterer or a polytheist.”

He said: “They are women known for adultery and men known for adultery, who became publicly infamous for adultery and were recognized by it. And people today who are in that position—whoever has had the prescribed punishment for adultery carried out upon him, or has become publicly known for adultery—it is not proper for anyone to marry him until repentance is known from him.”

key_terms.الزَّانِي: a man guilty of zina; here, one publicly known for adultery
key_terms.الزَّانِيَةُ: a woman guilty of zina; here, one publicly known for adultery
key_terms.تَوْبَةً: repentance that becomes manifest and recognized
key_terms.حَدُّ الزِّنَا: the prescribed legal punishment for zina

ai.seo_question: Can a person known for zina be married before their repentance is established?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as referring to men and women who are publicly known and infamous for zina. It indicates that one who has become known for zina, or upon whom the hadd of zina has been established, should not be married until sincere tawbah becomes evident.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4417 - It is narrated by Dawood bin Sirhan from Zurarah, who said that Abu Abdullah (as), was asked about the saying of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic:
"The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress does not marry except an adulterer or a polytheist." (Surah An-Nur 24:3)

Imam (as) said: "They are women known for adultery and men known for adultery, who have been publicly infamous for committing adultery and are recognized for it.
Today, people in such a situation, whether the prescribed punishment for adultery has been carried out on them or they are publicly known for adultery, should not be married until their repentance is established."
